messages:
incident-bot: Pager received — SEV2: downstream packet loss and BGP route oscillation observed for us-west-2 egress via AtlasTransit. Alerts from perf-mon: spike in TCP retransmits and 5xx for api.redwood.ai ~ 02:05 UTC
sre-alex: I'm on it. Paging oncall-net-jordan and net-priya. Anyone else?
oncall-net-jordan: here. grabbing peering dashboards. seeing a lot of AS-path churn on prefixes we announce to AtlasTransit (+ multiple withdraws). Latency to Atlas hop spikes to 250-400ms from edge.
net-priya: looking at BGP table from our IX routers. Confirming repeated flaps — communities stripped and our next-hop toggles between two upstreams. Splits on multiple paths.
infra-diego: high-level impact: ~12% of hosted traffic in us-west-2 hitting elevated error rates (mostly long tail customers), latency for embeddings increases. No control plane failures.
support-sam: Customer support tickets trickling in — two customers report 502s; others see degraded completion times.
net-priya: grabbing `vtysh` output now, partial:
```
BGP neighbor 203.0.113.45, ASN 64500, state Established
  Received prefixes: 24, withdraws: 12 in last 5m
  Last update: 02:06:41 UTC, AS path changes, MED toggles
```
sre-alex: any evidence of route-reflection loops or mis-announces from AtlasTransit?
net-priya: Looks like Atlas is re-advertising a subset of our prefixes with a shorter path to a downstream — causing traffic to hairpin across their network. They also sent a deaggregation of /22->/24s repeatedly.
oncall-net-jordan: mitigation plan: 1) Open ticket with AtlasTransit and escalate (doing now). 2) Temporarily prepend our AS to the problematic prefixes toward Atlas to prefer our other peer. 3) Shift critical traffic to secondary peer BluePipe via BGP community if possible. 4) Apply more aggressive route dampening for the affected neighborhood.
net-priya: I'm going to apply a temporary AS-prepend on the /22s toward Atlas and advertise a reduced-prefix aggregation to encourage stable selection. Applying on edge-router-egw3:
```
set policy community add 65535:10
route-map PREPEND-ATLAS permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list AFFECTED
  set as-path prepend 64510 64510
```
infra-diego: I'm standing by to add firewall/ACL changes if we need static route overrides for VIPs.
support-sam: flagging known-affected customers and updating status page: limited API failures in us-west-2, degraded latency. ETA unknown.
sre-alex: Atlas just acknowledged the ticket and says they will stop re-advertising deaggregates; they're seeing instability in their transit fabric. They requested we withdraw specific /24s while they stabilize.
oncall-net-jordan: proceeding to withdraw the deaggregated /24s and advertise the aggregate only. Doing withdrawal via router: `bgp withdraw 198.51.100.0/24` for the list.
net-priya: Withdraw completed, and prepends pushed. Monitoring route selection now. BGP churn drops significantly in the last 120s.
incident-bot: automated metric note: us-west-2 5xx rate dropped from 11% to 3% over 4m after mitigations :thumbsup:
support-sam: updating customers: status page updated, few customers replied: some see immediate improvement. Continuing to monitor.
sre-alex: handoff: @oncall-net-jordan, @net-priya — I'm stepping out for a follow-up call. Jordan take lead for next 2 hours, escalate to net-team if reoccurs.
oncall-net-jordan: roger. I'll keep monitoring route churn and will coordinate with Atlas for permanent fix. If instability returns, we'll shift primary egress to BluePipe and increase traffic steering.
net-priya: adding a follow-up item to the incident doc: ask Atlas for RCA and timeline for preventing deaggregation; request they flag our prefixes with a sticky community to prevent repairs.
infra-diego: ops note: no additional customer rollbacks required; we didn't need to failover to another region. Cost of path-change negligible.
support-sam: logging affected ticket IDs in the incident tracker and notifying CS managers.
sre-alex: final note before handoff: root cause suspected = AtlasTransit internal fabric causing repeated re-advertisements/deaggregation leading to AS-path oscillation; mitigations: AS-prepend + withdraw deaggregates + coordinate with Atlas. Recommend postmortem if customer impact > 10% for 10+ minutes.
oncall-net-jordan: acknowledged. I'll create incident postmortem and schedule a 30m bridge with Atlas and our net-team in 60m.
net-team: thanks all — keeping this thread for updates. closing temporary pager until further noise.
